review_candidates.description: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future. The IRC Yemen began its programs in October 2012. Since establishing its presence in the South of Yemen, in the Red Sea Coastal city of Aden, the organization has grown from just an implementing small project to handling large scale emergency and relief operations. Following the war which broke out in Yemen in March of 2015 and the humanitarian disaster, which was crafted by the same, IRC launched one an emergency response program in the southern governorates of Aden, Lahj, Abyan, Shabwah and Al Dhale, and expanded later in Sana’a and Hodeidah in the North. Currently IRC Yemen is operating in eight governorates in the south and north of Yemen through direct programming and through local partnerships, in Health, WASH, Nutrition, Economic Recovery Development, Education, Child Protection, Gender and Women Protection and Empowerment. The International Rescue Committee (IRC) have been working in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) for more than forty years. Today, the IRC has more than 2,200 staff working across the region, including in Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Syria, and Yemen to support those affected by some of the world’s most complex and protracted humanitarian crises. Scope Of Work The Field Manager leads IRC operations and program support in Shabwah and Abyan, ensuring effective, compliant, and secure field activities. The position also supervises field staff, oversees administrative functions, and contributes to strategic decision-making. This position is a member of the extended Senior Management Team and participates in all meetings and decision-making forums within IRC in line with his/her Job Description. Working Relations Position Reports to: Field Coordinator Position directly supervises: SC Officer, Humanitarian Access Officer, Finance/Admin Assistant. This position will also provide day-to-day administrative supervision for the most senior program staff from each sector. Other Internal And/or External Contacts Internal: Supply Chain, People & Culture, Program staff, Finance, Grants, Field support staff. External: UN agencies, partner organizations, local governance units, local communities. Ensure that all IRC premises — including the Shabwah sub-field office, in consultation with the Senior IT Officer on IT-related standards — meet IRC standards, and recommend improvements where necessary. Routinely communicate, coordinate and plan with the respective requesting staff/programs regarding the order and delivery of supplies. Ensure that IRC has adequate storage capacity for program supplies. Oversee vehicle operations and usage for the smooth and safe running of the programs. Maintain office records and disseminate information and correspondence between the field office and capital offices. Program Support Provide consistent and constructive support to all program departments in Shabwah and Abyan Governorates. Follow up with the sub-field office program staff to ensure quality programming is carried out for both direct implementation and partner implementation, and that IRC and donor expectations are met. Perform regular program site visits to ensure required progress and quality in implementation of activities. Partnership Responsibilities Work with Operations Management Team colleagues to support partners' capacity, ensuring adherence to IRC processes and agreed donor guidelines. Actively participate in Partnership Cycle Management, including partnership project opening, review, and closing meetings, capturing effective operational practices and lessons learned for future partnerships. Address any issues or misunderstandings which arise within the framework and spirit of IRC policies and rules of professional conduct. Support staff in the implementation of personnel policies, including performance evaluation, staff development, and disciplinary measures. Ensure attendance and leave management of all staff assigned to the Shabwah and Abyan sub-field offices, in close coordination with their capital-based managers. Compliance Ensure adherence to IRC policies and procedures across all operations departments, including Supply Chain, Humanitarian Access, People & Culture, Finance and IT. Ensure health, safety and security protocols are followed at all times, taking timely corrective action as required and in consultation with the Field Coordinator and SMT. Ensure that IRC SOPs and contingency plans are kept up to date and respected and enforce the same in the Shabwah and Abyan sub-field offices and throughout IRC implementation areas. Promptly inform the Field Coordinator of any areas of concern regarding potential or suspected violations of policies and procedures. Strategy and Program Approach Member of PWG, and co-responsible for delivering the functions of the PWG. Contribute to robust stakeholder analysis processes stakeholder analysis processes that enable the Strategy Action Plan (SAP) and each program design to be based on how we can best support, reinforce and complement local civil society, government and private sector actors. Member of PWG, and co-responsible for delivering the functions of the PWG, with respect to the relevant geographical area. Program Delivery Participate in due diligence processes and collaborative partnership risk management as appropriate. Participate in PCM, including to review successes, challenges, and lessons learned with the partner, and capturing effective finance practices for future partnerships. Assist with any security related local partner issues and coordinate with the partner on safe access.
